Implementation Plan

## Implementation plan: issue #7272. `RELEASE_TAGGING_ENABLED` stays default-on (activation gap from PR #7036 is a false positive)

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends agents.d fragment mechanism (`scripts/assemble_agents.py`)
Scope-mode justification: The clarify answer (Q1: B) chose to keep `RELEASE_TAGGING_ENABLED` default-on. That was the deliberate design in #7029. The changelog fragment `changelog.d/7029-release-validate-ci-gate.md` says: "New repository variable `RELEASE_TAGGING_ENABLED`, default `true`". The README row at line 245 says default `true`. The `tests/test_release_validate_ci_gate.py` docstring (line 8) says "default-on `RELEASE_TAGGING_ENABLED`", and its `SWITCH_ENV` (line 41) pins `|| 'true'`. The control that actually protects releases is the bounded `CI / lint` check-run gate (`scripts/release_ci_gate.sh`) in `validate` and `release`, and it fails closed. Flipping the default would add no protection. It would only stop every stable tag, GitHub Release and consumer dispatch until someone sets a repo variable, which goes against the agents.md rule that `_ENABLED` switches ship on and act as off switches. So the change is limited to one agents.d fragment that records the decision, so later activation checks stop reporting it. Workflows, README, tests and resolver logic are not touched. This is not Reduction mode: the approved answer itself replaces the issue's acceptance criterion.

### Planning ref
- `git rev-parse HEAD`: `eecbf75e90bef8b2acdcf06d05be773b270ece12`, branch `main`. No integration branch metadata; `Integration branch mismatch: unknown` (not `true`), so not blocked.

### Conflict detection
- The issue asks to "change both fallbacks and resolver defaults to false". The approved clarify answer (Q1: B) replaces that criterion with its own equivalence argument. The plan follows the answer.
- The issue's evidence is correct: `.github/workflows/mark-stable.yml:933` and `:936`, and `.github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml:6622` and `:6625`, use `vars.RELEASE_TAGGING_ENABLED || 'true'` and `${RELEASE_TAGGING_ENABLED-true}`. The code matches the documented intent; nothing is out of step.

### Automation / scheduler section (§20.E)
- No new script and no change to any existing script or workflow. This is a documentation fragment only.
- Scheduler / PR-push entry point: none new. The existing `static-checks` step in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (line ~249, `scripts/assemble_agents.py check --repo-root .` plus `tests/test_agents_fragment_contract.py`) validates the fragment on PR push. The release jobs fold it into `agents.md` later.
- No long-running supervisor is needed. No DB work. No registry entry in `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md`.

### 1. Files likely to change
- **Create:** `agents.d/7272-release-tagging-default-on.md`. This is the only file.
- **Do NOT change:** `.github/workflows/mark-stable.yml`, `.github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml`, `README.md`, `tests/test_release_validate_ci_gate.py`, `agents.md` (§25: no direct edits).

### 2. Functions or modules
None. Content of the fragment, in the shape of `agents.d/6712-weekly-consumer-backfill.md` (marker line first, then plain prose wrapped at about 78 columns):

```
<!-- agents: section="Immutable consumer wrapper pins" -->
- Release tagging switch defaults on (issue #7272, from #7029). In the
  `release` jobs of `mark-stable.yml` and `test-and-mark-stable.yml`,
  `RELEASE_TAGGING_ENABLED` resolves as `vars.RELEASE_TAGGING_ENABLED || 'true'`
  and `${RELEASE_TAGGING_ENABLED-true}`: unset, empty or `true` (any letter
  case) publishes, and any other value skips the changelog commit, tag pushes,
  release manifest build/attestation/upload, GitHub Release and consumer
  dispatch with a `::warning::`. This is intentional. The safety control is
  the fail-closed `CI / lint` check-run gate (`scripts/release_ci_gate.sh`)
  in `validate` and `release`; the switch is an operator's emergency off
  switch, and defaulting it off would only stop releases. Activation
  verification should not report the default-on fallback as a gap. To pause
  releases, set `RELEASE_TAGGING_ENABLED=false` and
  `AUTO_RELEASE_STABLE_ENABLED=false`.
```

The section heading `## Immutable consumer wrapper pins` exists in agents.md (line 1663), and it already documents the release jobs of `mark-stable.yml` / `test-and-mark-stable.yml` (attested release manifest). Do not add ` new` to the marker.

### 3. Data structures affected
None.

### 4. API/interface changes
None. No env var, default, log prefix, workflow input or output changes.

## Decisions
### D1 — Keep `RELEASE_TAGGING_ENABLED` default-on and record the intent
- Chosen: Leave both workflows, the README and the contract tests unchanged. Add an agents.d fragment saying default-on is intentional and the activation gap is a false positive.
- Alternatives considered: (A) Flip both fallbacks to `false` and update the README and tests. (C) Option A plus skipping `auto-release-stable.yml` re-dispatch while tagging is off. Or close the issue with a comment and no file change.
- Why: The approved clarify answer Q1: B. #7029 documented default `true`. The `CI / lint` gate gives the protection. agents.md forbids defaulting an `_ENABLED` switch off only so that a person has to turn it on. A and C would stop every stable release and consumer update. A fragment stops the same false positive from coming back from activation verification, which a comment alone would not do.

### D2 — Fragment target section
- Chosen: `Immutable consumer wrapper pins`.
- Alternatives considered: `Workflow architecture`, or a new section.
- Why: That section already covers what the stable release jobs publish (manifest, dispatch). Adding a new section needs ` new` and makes agents.md bigger for no gain.

## Security considerations
- Trust boundaries: none touched. No workflow, token, permission or script changes.
- Authorization: no new endpoints or surfaces.
- External input: none. The fragment is static text written by the pipeline.
- Abuse cases: someone might read the note as "tagging can't be turned off". The text says how to turn it off (`RELEASE_TAGGING_ENABLED=false`, plus `AUTO_RELEASE_STABLE_ENABLED=false`). The real safeguard against releasing a broken commit, the `CI / lint` gate, is unchanged and still fails closed. Money handling: not applicable.

### 5. Risks and edge cases
- If the fragment's section marker does not match an existing `##` heading exactly, `assemble_agents.py check` fails CI. Copy the heading text exactly: `Immutable consumer wrapper pins`.
- `scripts/check_agents_md_direct_edits.py` would fail if agents.md were edited directly. Only the fragment is added.
- The fragment must not contain `Fixes/Closes/Resolves #N` aimed at a tracking issue (§21). #7272 is a standalone activation-fix issue (not `ai:orchestrator-tracking`), so the PR body may use `Closes #7272`. Still run `scripts/lint_pr_body_auto_close.py` before opening the PR.
- Changelog: there is no user-visible behaviour change, so no `changelog.d/` fragment is required. If the implement or CI contract asks for one per PR, add `changelog.d/7272-release-tagging-default-on.md` with a single `<!-- changelog: docs -->`-style note that says nothing changed in behaviour.

### 6. Testing considerations
- Run `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 scripts/assemble_agents.py check --repo-root .`. It should exit 0 with the fragment folding into the named section.
- Run `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_agents_fragment_contract.py tests/test_assemble_agents.py tests/test_check_agents_md_direct_edits.py`.
- Run `tests/test_release_validate_ci_gate.py` unchanged. It should still pass, which shows the default-on contract was left alone.
- `git diff --stat` should show exactly one new file under `agents.d/`.

### 7. Pre-execution self-check
- Every factual reference was checked on the current ref: changelog line, workflow lines 933/936/6622/6625, README line 245, the test docstring and `SWITCH_ENV`, the agents.md heading at line 1663, the fragment format, and the CI `check` step.
- The plan follows the approved answer and changes no behaviour.
